name: Fix a pod rejected by a quota
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Drill EVERY corner of namespace resource governance harder than the exam: compute ResourceQuota, object-count quota, scoped quota (BestEffort), LimitRange defaults, LimitRange min/max bounds, ratio limits, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix of a pod rejected by a quota. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod rejected by the quota
questions.teach:
When a compute quota exists, a pod whose container omits a tracked dimension is **refused at admission** — so a Deployment's pod never gets created and it stays `0/1`. `kubectl -n <ns> get replicaset` / `describe rs` surfaces the error `must specify limits.cpu` (or similar).

**Gotcha:** fix the **Deployment's pod template** to declare the missing requests/limits — don't touch the quota.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `shipit` in `ckad-quotas` is stuck at `0/1` — its pods are **rejected by `compute-quota`** because the container doesn't declare all required resources. Diagnose the rejection and fix the Deployment's pod template so a pod is admitted and the Deployment reports an available replica. Don't change the quota; don't delete and rebuild.

Target: Deployment `shipit` has at least 1 available replica.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ckad-quotas describe rs -l app=shipit` → `failed quota: ... must specify limits.cpu,limits.memory,requests.cpu,requests.memory`. Edit the Deployment to add a full `resources` block (e.g. requests 100m/64Mi, limits 200m/128Mi), then watch `rollout status`.
questions.solution:
# The container declares no resources, so compute-quota refuses it.
kubectl -n ckad-quotas patch deployment shipit --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources","value":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"64Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"200m","memory":"128Mi"}}}]'
kubectl -n ckad-quotas rollout status deployment/shipit

verification.description: Deployment shipit has >=1 available replica (quota-rejection fixed in the pod template)

questions.eli5:
A Deployment is like a manager who's been told "always keep 1 worker on the floor." The manager (Deployment) doesn't hire directly — it tells a staffing agency (the **ReplicaSet**), which actually sends people (pods) to the door. But the building has that breaker-box rule (the **compute quota**): nobody gets in without declaring how much power they reserve and their spike limit.

Deployment `shipit` is stuck at `0/1` — zero workers on the floor. The worker it keeps sending has **no resource declaration**, so the doorman keeps bouncing them. The manager looks fine from the outside; the rejection is happening one layer down at the staffing agency.

To see the real reason you have to ask the ReplicaSet: `kubectl -n ckad-quotas describe rs -l app=shipit`. Down in its events you'll find `failed quota: compute-quota: must specify limits.cpu,limits.memory,requests.cpu,requests.memory`.

The fix is to give the **Deployment's pod template** a full `resources` block (e.g. requests 100m/64Mi, limits 200m/128Mi). The Deployment rolls out a new template, the new pod declares everything, the doorman lets it in, and `shipit` reaches `1/1`.

**Watch out for:**

- **Fix the pod template, not the quota.** The task forbids changing or deleting the quota — the pod is wrong, not the rule.
- The error hides **one layer down**. `kubectl get deploy` just shows `0/1`; you must `describe rs` (or check events) to see the quota rejection.
- You must declare **all four** dimensions — requests *and* limits, cpu *and* memory — or you'll just hit the same wall again.
- Don't delete and recreate the Deployment; patch/edit it in place so it rolls a new ReplicaSet.
- Your chosen values must also *fit* under the quota's remaining headroom.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a pod rejected by a compute quota

### Mental model
A Deployment owns a **ReplicaSet**, which owns **pods**. A compute ResourceQuota rejects pods at **admission** — so when a template is non-compliant, the pod is never created. The Deployment surface only shows `0/1`; the real error surfaces on the **ReplicaSet's events**, because that's the controller trying (and failing) to create the pod.

### The diagnosis chain
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-quotas get deploy shipit               # READY 0/1
kubectl -n ckad-quotas get rs -l app=shipit            # DESIRED 1, CURRENT 0
kubectl -n ckad-quotas describe rs -l app=shipit       # <-- the real error
# Events:  ... (combined from similar events):
#   Error creating: pods "shipit-..." is forbidden: failed quota: compute-quota:
#   must specify limits.cpu,limits.memory,requests.cpu,requests.memory
# also visible via:
kubectl -n ckad-quotas get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -i quota
```
Confirm the quota tracks compute:
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-quotas describe quota compute-quota
```

### Why the pod is missing (not just failing)
| Layer | What you see |
|---|---|
| Deployment | `0/1 available` — no error here |
| ReplicaSet | `FailedCreate` events naming the quota |
| Pod | **does not exist** — admission blocked it pre-creation |

This is different from a crash: there's no pod to `logs`/`describe`. Follow the owner chain down.

### The fix — edit the template, not the quota
Add a full `resources` block to the Deployment's pod template. Options:

Patch (JSON, targets container 0):
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-quotas patch deployment shipit --type=json -p='[{
  "op":"add",
  "path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources",
  "value":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"64Mi"},
           "limits":{"cpu":"200m","memory":"128Mi"}}}]'
```
Or `kubectl -n ckad-quotas edit deployment shipit` and add under the container:
```yaml
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi }
          limits:   { cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi }
```
Then watch it recover:
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-quotas rollout status deployment/shipit
kubectl -n ckad-quotas get deploy shipit               # 1/1
```

### Alternative fix
Instead of editing every Deployment, a **LimitRange** with `default`/`defaultRequest` in the namespace would auto-inject the missing values. But this task says fix the Deployment's template — do that.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Don't touch the quota** and **don't delete/recreate** the Deployment — patch/edit in place.
- The error is **not** on the Deployment or on any pod (there is none) — look at the **ReplicaSet** or namespace **events**.
- Declare **all four** dimensions; omitting one re-triggers the same rejection.
- Editing the template rolls a **new ReplicaSet**; the old `0`-replica RS may linger harmlessly.
- Chosen values must fit under the quota's remaining headroom, else you trade a "must specify" error for an "exceeded quota" error.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-quotas describe rs -l app=shipit        # find: failed quota ...
kubectl -n ckad-quotas patch deployment shipit --type=json -p='[{"op":"add",
  "path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources",
  "value":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"64Mi"},
           "limits":{"cpu":"200m","memory":"128Mi"}}}]'
kubectl -n ckad-quotas rollout status deployment/shipit
```
